findings.message: The 'second player waits' tests never use a waiting player who outranks the channeller under the closest-then-lowest-id rule. In packages/simulation/src/claim/claim.test.ts every waiter is farther away ('runs one channel at a time': b at x+1; 'lets a waiting player start...': b at x+100) or ties with a higher id ('keeps the protection of a protected player who must wait': b vs a, both at the claim point). The seeded invariants in determinism.test.ts check that the channeller is eligible and that progress === tick - startTick. Both would still hold if a closer or lower-id newcomer took over the channel. So an implementation that re-applied the ordering rule on every tick and preempted the active channel would pass the whole suite. Add a scripted case where a closer or lower-id eligible player arrives mid-channel and assert that the channel owner and progress are unchanged.
findings.requirement: Only one channel is active at a time; a second eligible player must wait.

findings.message: Non-mutation is tested for the claim state and the tick snapshot, but not for the config. The step() helper in packages/simulation/src/claim/claim.test.ts deep-freezes the input and the state and compares hashState(state) before and after. The ClaimConfig passed to stepClaim is never frozen or compared in any test, including the determinism.test.ts runs. A step that wrote to config (for example to claimPoint) would go undetected.
